thread.title: Ortitay and Fleming introduce bill to fund Pennsylvania's early literacy law
thread.title_full: Ortitay and Fleming introduce bill to fund Pennsylvania's early literacy law

author: d. n. ashby
title: Ortitay and Fleming introduce bill to fund Pennsylvania's early literacy law
text:
Rep. Jason Ortitay and Rep. Justin Fleming introduced the Keystone Literacy Investment Tax Credit on May 27, a bipartisan proposal aimed at funding Pennsylvania’s structured literacy law without raising taxes or increasing state spending.
House Bill 2541 would allow the state to raise up to $150 million by selling insurance premium tax credits through a competitive bidding process. The funds generated would be placed in a dedicated account for the Pennsylvania Department of Education, which would then award grants to school districts for evidence-based reading instruction. The tax credits could not be used until 2029, are capped at $50 million per year, and will expire after 2034, resulting in no impact on this year’s budget.
“The hard part is done,” Ortitay said. “Last November we passed one of the most significant education reforms in Pennsylvania in years. Now we have to give schools the tools to actually make it happen.” He added, “This is how you finish the job. We already made the decision to fix how Pennsylvania kids learn to read. This gives schools the resources to actually do it. Long-term return on kids who can read is one of the best investments government can make.” Fleming said, “Making sure our kids know how to read well is a bipartisan issue, as reading is the foundation of every other subject in school from word problems in math to history and science. This is a smart, fiscally responsible way to make sure the reform we passed last year actually works. I’m proud to join Rep. Ortitay in getting this done.” Ortitay also said, “Gov. Shapiro ran on a platform of getting things done,” adding that House Bill 2541 provides funding that is fiscally responsible and bipartisan.
Ortitay hopes that House Bill 2541 will be included during this year’s budget negotiations.
Ortitay chairs the House Communications and Technology Committee and serves on the House Education Committee; he also founded Jason’s Cheesecake Company and resides with his wife Amanda and daughters Delaney and Isabella, according to the official website .
